newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bomb contained UVF-type explosive - police.
newsitem.headline: Irish bomb contained UVF-type explosive - police.

text.p: Irish police said on Wednesday that a bomb found in Monaghan town on Monday contained a type of explosive used previously by pro-British Protestant guerrillas.
A report in the Irish Times newspaper blamed Protestant Loyalists in Northern Ireland for the failed attack on offices of Sinn Fein, the political wing of the IRA.

Security arrangements along the border with Northern Ireland were likely to be reassessed after the discovery of the device which the paper reported was "believed to have been planted by members of the UVF (Ulster Volunteer Force)".

"We can confirm that it was an explosive device," a police spokesman said. "We can confirm that the substance found on March 3 was Powergel 900 commercial explosive which is used in the mining industry."
Security analysts in Northern Ireland said that Powergel was used by UVF guerrillas in several bombs before banned Loyalists, fighting to uphold British rule, called a truce in October 1994.
The Monaghan bomb was taken away for examination late on Monday after a day-long security operation by Irish army disposal experts. Only the detonator exploded.
"This was the first Loyalist bomb attack in the Republic since September 1994 , although a number of hoax devices were planted last summer," wrote Irish Times security correspondent Jim Cusack.
"Higher levels of security along the border are likely to be considered now that the Loyalists have actually moved explosive into the Republic," he said.
No organisation has claimed responsible for the bomb.
Irish security forces have been on alert for Loyalist incursions since the IRA ended a 17 month ceasefire a year ago.

Multi-party talks in Belfast on the future of Northern Ireland, which exclude the IRA's Sinn Fein political arm, were expected to be adjourned later on Wednesday to allow parties to prepare for an election to be called in Britain and Northern Ireland by May.
